note: The Law-Backed Seam register (tempdoc 555 Pillar A). The SINGLE allowlist of pure, branch/arithmetic-dense, high-blast-radius logic whose failure mode is a silent WRONG VALUE (not an exception). Each seam declares its `law` (the invariant a property test must encode — Pillar B) and its `guard` (the test(s) that must kill faults in it — Pillar C). This file is the single authority that (1) scopes PIT `targetClasses` per module via the `conventions.mutation` plugin, and (2) is ratcheted per-seam on mutation test-strength by the `test-efficacy` discipline gate. Out-of-register code (IO / native / DTO / UI / gRPC plumbing) has no law and is NOT mutation-targeted by design (tempdoc 555 §6 Wall 2). Keep this register SMALL — only genuine law-bearing seams (AHA: do not over-DRY).
strengthMetric: test-strength = (KILLED + TIMED_OUT) / (KILLED + TIMED_OUT + SURVIVED), integer percent — matches PIT's own definition (TIMED_OUT counts as killed). NOT raw mutation score (tempdoc 555 §9.1). A per-seam noCoverage CEILING is ratcheted alongside so a seam cannot rot by adding untested branches (invisible to killed/covered).
propertyTestNote: The `*PropertyTest` guard tests are fixed-seed JUnit loops over generated inputs, NOT a true PBT framework: they give reproducibility but NO shrinking and a FIXED input sample (same inputs every run), so they are weaker than jqwik-style PBT. This is a deliberate supply-chain tradeoff — jqwik 1.10.0 shipped an AI-agent-targeted prompt-injection payload, so it is not added to this dependency-verified build (tempdoc 555 §7/§10). Mutation adequacy (the test-efficacy gate) is what actually certifies these tests bite.

seams.law: RRF: each leg's fused contribution is weight/(k+rank) — rank-monotone (strictly increases as a hit's rank improves) and weight-bounded to [0,1] (clamped). The result comparator is a TOTAL ORDER (deterministic docId tiebreak). CC/CC3: normalizeScore = (s-min)/range is score-monotone within a leg. The bm25 score-boost weight is non-negative and the fused score is monotone non-decreasing in it.
seams.note: The lead seam (tempdoc 555 §9.2). Pure (858 LOC, 0 native/IO refs). Tempdoc 554's #1 PBT target — the property (law) and mutation (bite) halves coincide here.

seams.law: calculateLineNumber(content, offset) = 1 + count('\n' in content[0, min(offset, len))); it is 1 for offset<=0 and non-decreasing in offset. findPrecedingHeading returns the LAST markdown heading (#{1,6} + text) starting before the offset, or NONE.
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from ChunkDocumentWriter (tempdoc 555 §4/§10 U4 — genuinely IO-entangled seam). Drives RAG chunk line/heading metadata; a silent off-by-one mis-attributes citations.

seams.law: Priority-ordered freshness classification: path-identity > file-kind > size > mtime > file-key. The FIRST difference in that order decides the result; null file-key on either side never triggers FILE_KEY_CHANGED. A reorder or flipped comparison silently misclassifies a changed file as FRESH (index corruption).
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from FileFreshnessSnapshot (IO capture stays in the record).

seams.law: Total, injective mapping from a post-snapshot SourceValidationResult to its ingestion reason code; every change kind maps to a distinct code. A swapped/dropped arm emits a misleading stale diagnostic.
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from WorkerIngestionAuthority (the IO admit() short-circuit stays in the authority).

seams.law: Total, injective mapping from an OCR attempt's baseline quality to its OcrSkipReason; baselineQuality>0 maps to TEXTUAL (existing text was adequate), every other case maps to NO_TEXT_FOUND (OCR was attempted and found nothing). A swapped/reused arm silently conflates a routing decision with an extraction failure and indexes a document with no body content and no honest diagnostic (tempdoc 671).
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from PolicyDrivenTikaExtractor (the IO-heavy OCR-engine calls stay in the extractor), mirroring the admission-policy seam's shape for the same failure mode in a sibling package.

seams.law: Total, injective mapping from an extraction attempt's (content, truncated) facts to its ExtractionStatus; blank content maps to SUCCESS_EMPTY regardless of truncated, non-blank+truncated maps to SUCCESS_PARTIAL, non-blank+untruncated maps to SUCCESS_FULL. A swapped/reused arm silently claims full success for a document with no usable content — the same failure mode as ocr-outcome-classifier, one level more foundational (tempdoc 671, Long-term design part 2).
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from ExtractionArtifact.full (both overloads) — the cross-extractor, already-indexed trust/provenance field, not OCR-specific. Confirmed via live testing to affect any empty document (plain text, third-party extractor plugins), not just scans.

seams.law: Total mapping from a ledger transition's artifactStatus string to its success bucket (FULL/PARTIAL/EMPTY); "SUCCESS_PARTIAL" maps to PARTIAL, "SUCCESS_EMPTY" maps to EMPTY, every other value (including null and unrecognized/legacy strings) maps to FULL. A swapped/reused arm silently reproduces the extraction-outcome-classifier's conflation one layer up, at the ingestion-boundary altitude, even after ExtractionStatus itself is fixed (tempdoc 671, Long-term design part 2).
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from IngestionOutcomeJournal.drainPending's inline isPartialSuccessTransition boolean (the IO-heavy ledger drain/write stays in the journal). The second, wider-scoped consumer the confidence-building pass found undertraced before implementation started.

seams.law: delay = min(base * 2^consecutiveFailures, cap); exponential in the failure count, clamped to the cap, non-decreasing in failures, negatives clamped. An off-by-one exponent or wrong cap comparison causes retry starvation or thundering-herd thrashing.
seams.note: Functional-core extraction from BackfillScheduler (the System.currentTimeMillis next-retry timestamp stays in the scheduler).

seams.law: belowFloor(lapFloor, contrastFloor) = laplacianVariance < lapFloor AND rmsContrast < contrastFloor — strictly conjunctive, never either-signal-alone. A flip to OR would abstain on pure noise (high Laplacian variance, low real signal) or on sparse-but-legible text (low contrast alone), defeating VDU's purpose of reading documents OCR already failed on (tempdoc 677 Stage 0 CAUTION).
seams.note: Tempdoc 677 S3: the input-legibility signal underlying VduAbstentionGate's Stage 0. Deferred from the prior (S3) slice; registered here per this slice's item 6.

seams.law: inputVerdict rejects iff LegibilityMeasures.belowFloor(LAPLACIAN_FLOOR, CONTRAST_FLOOR). outputVerdict rejects iff (meanLogprob != null AND meanLogprob < MEAN_LOGPROB_FLOOR) OR (lowConfidenceFraction != null AND lowConfidenceFraction > LOW_CONFIDENCE_FRACTION_CEILING) OR (finishReason != null AND finishReason NOT IN {"stop", "length"}). A null meanLogprob/lowConfidenceFraction (NO SIGNAL) must NEVER itself contribute to rejection — only the finish-reason arm may still fire. A silent flip of any comparison either indexes fabricated text as real content (false pass) or discards genuinely legible extractions (false abstain) — tempdoc 677's core defect.
seams.note: Tempdoc 677 Stages 0+1: the abstention cascade's verdict logic, consumed by VduProcessor/VduBatchProcessor (the IO-heavy model-call orchestration and aggregation stay in VduProcessor).

seams.law: classify(content) = EMPTY iff content is null/blank; TRIVIAL iff non-blank with fewer than MIN_USABLE_ALPHANUMERIC_CHARS (=2, measured) letters-or-digits; NONE otherwise. The mapping is total and the threshold is the largest value with a zero false-positive rate against the ohr-bench-clean legitimate-content floor (min legitimate content = 2 alphanumerics). Raising it silently marks legitimate short documents as unreadable holes and burns GPU fallback budget on them; lowering it to 0 re-opens the silent-empty-index defect this seam exists to close.
seams.note: Tempdoc 790 item 1: the trigger side of the extraction dropout fallback chain (structured -> OCR -> VDU). Consumed by PolicyDrivenTikaExtractor (tier-1 gate), VisualRoutingDecision (tier-2 gate) and IndexingDocumentOps (honest-hole marker).

seams.law: permitsTier(t) iff 1 <= t <= maxFallbackTiers (tier 0 = structured extraction is never charged); exhausted(elapsedMs) iff elapsedMs >= perDocBudgetMs (boundary inclusive); permitsTierNow(t, elapsedMs) = permitsTier(t) AND NOT exhausted(elapsedMs). Negative bounds are rejected, never clamped. A silent widening lets one pathological document consume unbounded OCR/GPU time; a silent narrowing disables the fallback chain that recovers empty extractions.
seams.note: Tempdoc 790 item 2: the per-document bound on the dropout fallback chain, nested inside TimeboxedContentExtractor's whole-extraction timeout.

seams.law: compute(plan, contract, declined) classifies each required file against three authorities. USER INTENT first: a file or plan-skip whose packageId is in `declined` is DECLINED, in BOTH plan positions (downloads, for a plan computed without the set; skipped(), for one computed with it). Otherwise a file the plan still wants to download is MISSING_CONTRACTED iff the contract's entry for its package is present, NOT skipped-kind, and lists that exact filename in installedFiles; otherwise MISSING_UNCONTRACTED. Only MISSING_* is a gap: installedFully() = something installed AND no MISSING_CONTRACTED AND (a contract exists OR nothing is missing); repairNeeded() = any required file missing at all, INDEPENDENT of contractedness; optionalGaps() = the non-required MISSING_*. pendingRegistryAdditions() = the MISSING_UNCONTRACTED package ids, deduped. A DECLINED file is recorded in files() and read by no truth claim: the user-facing authority on declines is the per-component `declined` flag on the plan preview, so this computation names no decline list of its own (a second one would be a fork of a live preference this pure function cannot see). Widening 'contracted' to package granularity (or to skipped-kind entries) makes a newer version's added artifact read as retroactive non-installation (round-10 F2 / round-11 F4); narrowing repairNeeded to contracted gaps only hides the round-11 consequence entirely (an upgraded machine loses GPU for every ONNX encoder while the status claims a complete install). Counting a DECLINED file as a gap leaves every user who switched a component off permanently reading 'Not Installed' plus a Repair prompt; reading the contract's historical SkipCause.USER_DECLINED instead of the CURRENT declined set freezes that decision forever, so a re-enabled component never becomes an offerable gap again.
seams.note: Tempdoc 805 G.3 W-TRUTH: the file-granularity install-completeness decision consumed by AiInstallService.applyInstalledFromPlan for installedFully / pendingRegistryAdditions / repairNeeded. Three authorities meet here: registry x profile (what is required), disk via the planner's already-installed probe (what is present), the install contract (what was installed).

seams.law: record(docId, content, total, from, windows) folds a slice into the document's running sum ONLY when from == the tracked resume point and the content fingerprint matches; it returns the new resume point. complete(docId) = L2Normalize(sum / windowsAccumulated), which is exactly OnnxEmbeddingEncoder.meanPoolChunks over the same windows, and drops the entry. nextWindow(docId, content) = 0 whenever nothing is tracked OR the fingerprint differs. Every failure here is a silent WRONG VECTOR that indexes cleanly: double-counting a slice (accepting a non-matching from) skews the mean, blending two content revisions embeds a document that never existed, and a resume point that does not advance re-embeds windows forever.
seams.note: Round-15 post-round finding: the cross-cycle accumulator that lets a long document's windowed embedding resume instead of restarting every scheduler cycle.

seams.law: A window is scored; a SOURCE is reported. For every prepared request: 0 <= windowToSource[w] < sourceCount for every window w, windowDocIds[w] == chunkDocIds[windowToSource[w]], and suppliedBySource[i] is true iff passageTexts[i] was non-blank. split() tiles a passage into non-overlapping windows of at most WINDOW_CHARS whose concatenation is the passage (the tail is never dropped). admissionCap(sentences, deadlineMs) = max(1, floor(deadlineMs/UNIT_COST_MS)/max(1,sentences)) and the admitted window count never exceeds it, never exceeds windowsConsidered, and keeps at least one window per text-bearing source while slots remain.
seams.note: Tempdoc 836 §1.3 — windowing adds a SECOND ordinal space beside the one the wire reports, which is the F-049 shape. A back-map slip silently attributes a claim to the wrong source; an admission slip silently scores work the Head has already abandoned (§3.4, measured 49.8s for a discarded result).

seams.law: estimate(totalBytes) returns Estimate.UNKNOWN (both fields -1, the 'no honest basis' sentinel) on EVERY arm that cannot support a reading: fewer than minSamples samples; a stalled series (now - newest.atNanos > stallNanos); a window shorter than minSpanNanos or non-positive; and a window over which deltaBytes <= 0. Otherwise bytesPerSecond = deltaBytes * 1e9 / spanNanos over the retained window, and remainingSeconds = round(max(0, totalBytes - newest.bytes) / bytesPerSecond) — except that totalBytes <= 0 yields a KNOWN rate with an unknown (-1) horizon, because rate and horizon are independently knowable. remainingSeconds == 0 is a VALUE (nothing left), never the sentinel; consumers must test rateKnown()/remainingKnown() before reading either field. sample() drops a negative reading, CLEARS the series when the cumulative count moves backwards (a fetch restarting a file from zero after an integrity failure is not the same monotone progression, and carrying the old baseline through the drop reports a rate that never happened), evicts samples older than windowNanos while always retaining at least one, and caps retention at MAX_SAMPLES. The clock is an injected monotonic nanos supplier — never wall-clock — so an adjustment mid-download cannot produce a negative span or an absurd rate.
seams.note: Tempdoc 840 U1 — the backend half of the missing download ETA. The failure mode is exactly this register's class: every wrong answer here is a plausible NUMBER rendered to the user on a multi-GB download, not an exception. Collapsing any UNKNOWN arm to 0 is the specific defect — it renders as '0 B/s' or '0s left' on a transfer that is merely young, stalled, or unmeasured, which is the most confident lie the surface can tell. Sibling of windowed-embed-progress: stateful progress arithmetic whose state is fed only by samples and an injected clock, with no IO.
